content.title: About
content.content: Brandy Alexander is a classic cocktail made of brandy, dark crème de cacao and cream. It is usually served in a cocktail glass and garnished with grated nutmeg. The flavor combines the sweetness of cream, the bitterness of chocolate and the aroma of brandy.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The drink was created in the early 1920s and named after Russian Emperor Alexander III.
The original recipe used cognac, later replaced by generic brandy.
Brandy Alexander appears frequently in literature and film, for example in the movie “Casablanca”.
Grated nutmeg used for garnish gives the drink its distinctive aroma.
Variations include substituting ice cream for cream or adding vanilla syrup.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Dark crème de cacao provides flavonoids that help combat free radicals.

items.title: Source of vitamin B2
items.content: Brandy, like other spirits, contains small amounts of riboflavin, important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Moderate consumption can be relaxing
items.content: Alcohol in modest amounts has a calming effect on the nervous system.

items.title: Alcohol content
items.content: Brandy Alexander contains alcohol, so it is not recommended for pregnant women, children, or people with liver problems.

items.title: High calorie count
items.content: Cream and sugar make the cocktail calorie‑dense; moderation is important for weight management.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: Those with lactose intolerance or dairy allergy should replace cream with a plant‑based alternative.

content.title: How to Drink
content.content: Serve the cocktail chilled in a cocktail glass, garnished with grated nutmeg. It can be enjoyed as a dessert drink after dinner or as a festive toast.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Ingredients (brandy, crème de cacao, cream) should be stored separately: brandy and crème de cacao in a cool, dark place; cream in the refrigerator and used within a few days after opening.
